facts.statement: Rahonavis lived in northwestern Madagascar during the Late Cretaceous period, approximately 70 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Rahonavis is a genus of bird-like theropod from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian, from about 70 to 66 mya) of what is now northwestern Madagascar.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Rahonavis, a partial skeleton cataloged as UA 8656, was discovered by Catherine Forster and colleagues in the Maevarano Formation near Berivotra, Madagascar.
facts.quote: It is known from a partial skeleton (UA 8656) found by Catherine Forster and colleagues in Maevarano Formation rocks at a quarry near Berivotra, Mahajanga Province.

facts.statement: Rahonavis was a small predator measuring about 70 cm in length and weighing between 0.45 and 2.27 kg, featuring a raised sickle claw on its second toe.
facts.quote: Rahonavis was a small predator, at about 70 cm long and 0.45-2.27 kg (1-5 lbs), with the typical dromaesaurid-like raised sickle claw on the second toe.

facts.statement: Rahonavis was approximately one-fifth larger than Archaeopteryx, making it about the size of a modern raven.
facts.quote: Rahonavis was one-fifth larger than the closely related Archaeopteryx, about the size of a modern raven.

facts.statement: Fossils of Rahonavis were first recovered in 1995 by a joint expedition from SUNY and the University of Antananarivo near the village of Berivotra, Madagascar.
facts.quote: The fossilized remains of Rahonavis were first recovered from the Maevarano Formation in Madagascar in 1995 by a joint expedition of SUNY and the University of Antananarivo, near the village of Berivotra.

facts.statement: The discoverers originally named the genus Rahona but renamed it Rahonavis after finding that Rahona was already used for a genus of moths.
facts.quote: The discoverers of Rahonavis initially named it Rahona but changed the name after discovering that the name Rahona was already assigned to a genus of lymantriid moths.

facts.statement: Rahonavis was a small predator about the size of an Archaeopteryx, roughly 70 cm long and weighing 0.45 to 2.27 kg, with a typical Velociraptor-like sickle claw on the second toe.
facts.quote: Rahonavis fue un pequeño predador, de alrededor del tamaño de un Archaeopteryx con unos 70 centímetros de largo y 0,45-2,27 kilogramos, con la típica garra falciforme de un Velociraptor en el segundo dedo del pie.

facts.statement: Rahonavis possessed a long tail, a jaw crowned with serrated teeth, and the characteristic retractable claw on the second toe typical of dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: Tenía una larga cola, una mandíbula coronada de dientes aserrados y una característica típica de los dromeosáuridos, la garra retráctil en el segundo dedo.

facts.statement: Evidence of feathers on the ulna gave Rahonavis an avian appearance.
facts.quote: Sobre la ulna hay evidencia de presencia de plumas lo que le daba una apariencia de ave.

facts.statement: There has been historical uncertainty regarding whether Rahonavis belongs to the bird clade Avialae or is a closely related dromaeosaurid.
facts.quote: Rahonavis has historically been the subject of some uncertainty as to its proper taxonomic position – whether it is a member of the clade Avialae (birds) or a closely related dromaeosaurid.

facts.statement: As of 2020, paleontologists remain undecided whether Rahonavis is an unenlagiine, a dromaeosaurid, or an avialan.
facts.quote: As of 2020, it is undecided among paleontologists whether the paravian Rahonavis is an unenlagiine, a dromaeosaurid, or an avialan.

facts.statement: Despite artistic depictions showing flight, it is unclear if Rahonavis could fly, and some doubt exists regarding whether the forearm material with quill knobs belongs to the same skeleton as the rest of the remains.
facts.quote: Although numerous artists' reconstructions of Rahonavis show it in flight, it is not clear that it could fly; there has even been some doubt that the forearm material, which includes the quill knobs, belongs with the rest of the skeleton.

facts.statement: Luis M. Chiappe argued that Rahonavis could probably fly, citing its large, robust ulna and prominent quill knobs as evidence of larger and more powerful wings than those of Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: Chiappe maintained that Rahonavis could probably fly, noting that its ulna was large and robust compared to Archaeopteryx, and that this fact, coupled with the prominent quill knobs, suggest that Rahonavis had larger and more powerful wings than that earlier bird.

facts.statement: The name Rahonavis means "cloud menace bird," derived from the Malagasy words for cloud or menace combined with the Latin word for bird.
facts.quote: The name Rahonavis means, approximately, "cloud menace bird", from Malagasy (RA-hoo-na, "cloud" or "menace") + Latin "bird".

facts.statement: Agnolín and Novas (2013) suggested that, similar to Microraptor, Rahonavis likely used a bat-like flight stroke utilizing the deltoideus muscle complexes.
facts.quote: Agnolín and Novas (2013) noted that, like Microraptor, a bat-like flightstroke using the deltoideus complexes seems to have been likely in R. ostromi.

facts.statement: Rahonavis was discovered in 1995 in the Maevarano Formation by a joint expedition from SUNY and the University of Antananarivo near the village of Berivotra.
facts.quote: Rahonavis fue encontrado en 1995 en la Formación Maevarano por una expedición conjunta de la SUNY y la Universidad de Antananarivo cerca de la villa de Berivotra.

facts.statement: Rahonavis is known from a single skeleton consisting of articulated hind legs, torso, parts of the tail, and good remains of the forelimbs and shoulder bones.
facts.quote: Rahonavis es conocido por un solo esqueleto, consistiendo en las patas traseras, torso, partes de la cola todas ellas articuladas y buenos restos de los miembros anteriores y huesos del hombro.

facts.statement: Rahonavis was about one-fifth larger than Archaeopteryx, roughly the size of a modern crow.
facts.quote: Rahonavis era un quinto más grande que el Archaeopteryx, de alrededor del tamaño de un cuervo actual.

facts.statement: Rahonavis lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Rahonavis belongs to the parent group Unenlagiinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Unenlagiinae

facts.statement: Rahonavis is classified within the family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Dromaeosauridae

facts.statement: Rahonavis is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: There has been historical uncertainty regarding whether Rahonavis is a member of the clade Aves or closely linked to dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: Rahonavis ha estado históricamente sujeta a cierta incertidumbre sobre su correcta clasificación, entre sí es un miembro del clado Aves o estrechamente vinculado a los dromeosáuridos.

facts.statement: A 2013 analysis by Agnolin and Novas found Rahonavis closer to Avialae than to Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: Un gran análisis publicado por Agnolín y Novas en 2013 encontró a Rahonavis más cerca de Avialae que de Dromaeosauridae.

facts.statement: A 2019 analysis by Hartman et al. strongly rejected the avian position of Rahonavis, supporting its placement in Unenlagiinae as requiring fewer evolutionary steps.
facts.quote: El análisis de Hartman et al. de 2019 "rechazó enérgicamente" la supuesta posición aviana de Rahonavis, encuentra su ubicación en Unenlagiinae mejor apoyada ya que requiere 10 pasos menos.

facts.statement: Some researchers have suggested that Rahonavis represents a chimera combining the forelimb of a bird with the skeleton of a dromaeosaurid, leading them to consider the genus a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Algunos investigadores han sugerido que Rahonavis representa una quimera que consiste en el miembro superior de un pájaro combinado con el esqueleto de un dromeosáurido, y considera a Rahona como un nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Many other scientists, including the original describers, maintain that the remains belong to a single animal, citing the close proximity of the wing bones to the rest of the skeleton.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, muchos otros científicos, incluyendo los descriptores originales de Rahonavis, mantienen que sus restos pertenecen a un solo animal, citando la gran proximidad de los huesos del ala al resto del esqueleto.

facts.statement: The shoulder bones of Rahonavis show evidence of ligament insertions that allow the independent mobility necessary for flapping.
facts.quote: Adicionalmente, en Rahonavis los huesos del hombro muestran la evidencia de la inserción de ligamentos que permiten la movilidad independiente necesaria para el aleteo.

facts.statement: Chiappe concluded that Rahonavis was capable of flight, though it would have been clumsier in the air than modern birds.
facts.quote: Chiappe concluye que Rahonavis era capaz de volar, aunque habría sido más torpe en el aire que los pájaros modernos.

facts.statement: A dentary has been found associated with the holotype, although it is rarely described.
facts.quote: Se ha encontrado un dentario asociado con el holotipo, aunque rara vez se describe.

facts.statement: A solitary thoracic vertebra found in mid-Cretaceous sediments between the Albian and Cenomanian, approximately 100-99 million years ago in the Kem Kem region of Morocco (cataloged NMC 50852), is very similar to those of R. ostromi.
facts.quote: una vértebra torácica solitaria encontrada en sedimentos de mediados del Cretácico, entre el Albiense al Cenomaniense, hace aproximadamente 100-99 millones de años en la región de Kem Kem, Marruecos, catalogada NMC 50852, es muy similar a las de R. ostromi.

rejected.statement: From the early 2000s, a consensus emerged that Rahonavis was more closely related to deinonychosaurs than to birds, specifically placing it within the South American dromaeosaurid clade Unenlagiinae.
rejected.quote: Beginning in the early 2000s, a consensus emerged among most theropod researchers that Rahonavis was more closely related to deinonychosaurs than to avialans, and specifically was a member of the South American dromaeosaurid clade Unenlagiinae.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'that Rahonavis was more closely related to deinonychosaurs'

rejected.statement: Rahonavis shoulder bones show evidence of ligament attachments that allowed the independent mobility required for flapping flight.
rejected.quote: Additionally, Rahonavis shoulder bones show evidence of ligament attachments allowing the independent mobility needed for flapping flight.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Rahonavis shoulder bones show evidence of ligament attachments'

rejected.statement: The specific name R. ostromi was coined in honor of the paleontologist John Ostrom.
rejected.quote: The specific name, R. ostromi, was coined in honor of John Ostrom.
